requirements.requirement: The UI must conform to corporate UI standards for look-and-feel, component usage, and accessibility so it behaves like other corporate apps.
requirements.source_citation: the UI needs to look and behave like other corporate apps — we keep getting flagged in reviews for mismatched components and accessibility stuff — and, well, we really shouldn't be reinventing that every time.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder explicitly states the UI must match corporate standards and avoid mismatched components and accessibility failures; implies need for consistent styling, component libraries, and accessibility conformance. Gaps: which exact standards/versions, specific accessibility levels (e.g., WCAG AA) are not specified.
requirements.follow_up_question: Which corporate UI standard documents and accessibility level (e.g., WCAG 2.1 AA) should we target, and is there a shared component library we must use?

requirements.requirement: Routine screen-to-screen transitions must complete in approximately five seconds or less to provide a snappy user experience.
requirements.source_citation: maybe five seconds for those small transitions feels acceptable to me — any longer and people start switching tasks or calling in.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder gave an explicit performance target for small UI transitions (5s). Gap: which specific screens/actions qualify as 'small transitions' and whether this is median, average, or percentile SLA.
requirements.follow_up_question: Please list the common tasks/screens this 5s target applies to and which percentile (e.g., 95th) or average should be used for SLA measurement.

requirements.requirement: Transaction details displayed or used for authoritative dispute decisions must be traceable back to the Statement Database as the canonical source; caching is allowed for UX but authoritative reads must map to that DB.
requirements.source_citation: We are required to get transaction details straight from the Statement Database — like the canonical source. We can cache for UX reason, sure, but any authoritative data for dispute decisions has to be traceable back to that DB.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder mandates the Statement DB as source-of-truth and allows caching only for UX; emphasizes traceability for audit. Gaps: cache TTLs, validation strategy, and how mapping/traceability metadata should be recorded.
requirements.follow_up_question: What cache TTLs or invalidation rules are acceptable, and what metadata (e.g., source DB record ID, timestamp) must be stored to demonstrate traceability to the Statement Database?

requirements.requirement: Cardmember details must be obtained from the Cardmember Information Database as the authoritative source and be traceable to that system; caching may be used for UX but authoritative operations must validate against it.
requirements.source_citation: Same deal with cardmember details — those come from the Cardmember Information Database.
requirements.rationale: Mirror of the transaction-source requirement for cardmember data; stakeholder states the Cardmember DB is authoritative. Gaps: which fields are critical to validate and cache invalidation rules.
requirements.follow_up_question: Which specific cardmember fields require authoritative validation on write/critical operations, and what are the acceptable caching/invalidation policies for cardmember data?

requirements.requirement: The app must not change account balances locally; any financial adjustments must be submitted as requests to the Cardmember Posting and Billing System, and the app must listen for and record confirmations/status updates from that system.
requirements.source_citation: The app shouldn't change account balances itself. We send adjustment requests to the Cardmember Posting and Billing System and then that system applies them.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder clarifies system boundary and authoritative actor for financial adjustments; implies need for reliable request submission and reliable status handling. Gaps: expected confirmation latency, retry semantics, and failure handling protocol.
requirements.follow_up_question: What are the expected SLA/latency, retry behavior, and error-handling semantics for adjustment requests and confirmations from the Posting and Billing System?

requirements.requirement: Role-based access control must restrict who can create, modify, or view disputes and sensitive data; the backend must enforce role-based views and not rely solely on front-end hiding.
requirements.source_citation: There's also the whole access-control thing — not everyone should be able to kick off a dispute — and we need to keep a full history of everything a rep does on a case.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder emphasizes RBAC and backend enforcement due to past incident where front-end hiding failed; requires restricting actions and data visibility. Gaps: exact RBAC matrix, permission rules, and enforcement mechanisms.
requirements.follow_up_question: Please provide the required RBAC roles and a matrix of permissions (create, view, edit, close, override) for each role, and confirm backend enforcement mechanisms (e.g., API authorization checks).

requirements.requirement: Support a small set of role tiers (e.g., basic rep, senior rep, supervisor, admin, external partner) rather than many micro-roles.
requirements.source_citation: I think we'll need maybe a handful of tiers — basic rep, senior rep, supervisor, admin, and maybe an external partner role for merchant-facing people.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder proposes approximate RBAC roles; useful for scoping access control complexity. Gaps: exact responsibilities and whether additional sub-roles are needed over time.
requirements.follow_up_question: Are these the definitive roles to implement initially, and should the system support adding more roles or fine-grained permissions later?

requirements.requirement: The backend must enforce data masking and data segregation for external partners and other roles so sensitive fields are never exposed via APIs even if front-end hiding is bypassed.
requirements.source_citation: we need to hide or mask certain data and change what components are visible ... we can't just rely on front-end hiding; the back end must enforce the data separation too.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder requests backend-enforced masking for external partners to prevent accidental exposure; motivated by prior incident. Gaps: which fields require masking and masking rules (redaction, partial, hashed).
requirements.follow_up_question: Which specific data fields must be masked or redacted for external partners, and what masking policy (e.g., partial mask, remove entirely) is required per field?

requirements.requirement: The system must be effectively available 24/7 except for scheduled maintenance windows: Mon–Sat 03:00–04:00 ET and Sun 01:00–05:00 ET.
requirements.source_citation: The maintenance windows were documented as Monday through Saturday from 3:00 AM to 4:00 AM Eastern, and on Sunday from 1:00 AM to 5:00 AM Eastern. Outside those windows we expect it to be available.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder provided explicit maintenance windows and expectation of near-continuous availability outside those windows. Gaps: acceptable SLA percentage uptime and planned emergency maintenance behavior.
requirements.follow_up_question: What uptime SLA percentage (e.g., 99.9%) should we target outside the scheduled maintenance windows, and what is the process for emergency maintenance notifications?

requirements.requirement: The application must support 350 concurrent users at peak without observable degradation (no increased response times, timeouts, or error rates noticeable to users).
requirements.source_citation: Specifically, the stakeholder group that set requirements mentioned three hundred and fifty concurrent users as what we should support without degradation.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder gave a concrete concurrency target and definition for 'no degradation'. Gaps: workload mix, transactional intensity per user, and performance metrics to evaluate degradation.
requirements.follow_up_question: Please provide a profile of typical user activity (requests/sec per user, heavy vs light operations) so we can size load tests for 350 concurrent users.

requirements.requirement: Measure and monitor both response times (average and percentiles) for common tasks and error rates; define acceptable error-rate thresholds for operations and alert when exceeded.
requirements.source_citation: So we should track both — average and percentile response times for common tasks like opening a case and an acceptable error rate threshold that should not be exceeded.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder requests observability metrics (response times, percentiles, error rates) to determine degradation. Gaps: exact percentile targets (e.g., 95th), specific numeric error thresholds, and tooling for monitoring/alerting.
requirements.follow_up_question: Which percentiles (e.g., 95th, 99th) and numerical thresholds for response time and error rates should be considered acceptable for key operations?

requirements.requirement: Maintain an immutable audit trail recording who performed each action (user ID), when (timestamp), what changed (previous and new values), notes/correspondence, and links to outbound items/reference IDs so timelines can be replayed.
requirements.source_citation: it needs to have who did what and when, like user ID and timestamp, and what changed — so the previous value and the new value — plus any notes or correspondence attached to the action. Also, if an action triggers an outbound item, like a chargeback or an adjustment request, we need to log that linkage along with any reference IDs. ... That history can't be editable — we need immutable audit entries.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder explicitly lists required audit data and mandates immutability for compliance and replayability. Gaps: retention period, storage mechanism (append-only, WORM), and access controls for audit logs.
requirements.follow_up_question: What retention period and storage/legal protections (e.g., WORM storage) are required for audit logs, and who should be allowed to access them?

requirements.requirement: Design flows and recordkeeping to demonstrate compliance with credit card dispute regulations, including preserving records, meeting turnaround times, and specific wording in correspondence as required by legal.
requirements.source_citation: They insisted we design the flows so that we can show compliance if regulators ask, like keeping records, certain turnaround times, and specific wording in correspondence. ... compliance is non-negotiable.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder emphasizes regulatory compliance impacting timelines, records, and correspondence wording. Gaps: which specific regulations/rules apply and concrete timeline targets or wording templates.
requirements.follow_up_question: Can legal provide the specific regulatory requirements and templates (timelines, required wording, and recordkeeping obligations) we must implement and prove in audit?

requirements.requirement: Cached reads for performance are allowed, but when a dispute is formalized or escalated the system must re-fetch or validate cached data against the authoritative Statement DB (and Cardmember DB as applicable).
requirements.source_citation: cached data has to be validated or re-fetched when a dispute is formalized... make UX fast with cached reads but fall back to authoritative reads when creating or escalating a dispute.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder requires a caching strategy that trades UX speed with authoritative validation at critical operations. Gaps: validation timing, consistency guarantees (strong vs eventual), and methods (re-fetch, checksum, versioning).
requirements.follow_up_question: What validation mechanism should be used when re-fetching (full fetch, diffs, version checks), and must the authoritative read be synchronous before finalizing a dispute?

requirements.requirement: Avoid heavy synchronous calls to the Statement Database during peak; prefer caching patterns, batched retrievals, or other load-reducing strategies to comply with upstream constraints.
requirements.source_citation: The statement DB team warned us against hammering them with synchronous calls for heavy queries during peak; they asked for caching patterns or batched retrievals where possible.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder relays upstream constraint to limit synchronous heavy queries; implies need for batching/caching and careful integration design. Gaps: allowed call rates, batch sizes, and peak windows.
requirements.follow_up_question: What are the Statement DB team's acceptable call rate limits or recommended batch sizes/windows, and are there agreed throttling/backoff policies?

requirements.requirement: Pre-fill forms and minimize clicks by populating fields from the Cardmember DB where possible to reduce user effort and repetitive actions.
requirements.source_citation: reps hate extra clicks and repetitive forms — if we can pre-fill stuff from the cardmember DB and keep the flow short, they'll love us.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder requests usability improvements (pre-fill, fewer clicks) tied to using cardmember data for convenience. Gaps: which fields to pre-fill, consent/privacy concerns, and when pre-fill must be overridden.
requirements.follow_up_question: Which specific form fields should be pre-filled from the Cardmember DB, and are there privacy/consent rules about when pre-filled data must be hidden or confirmed by the rep?

requirements.requirement: Ensure reliable status synchronization after the Sunday maintenance window (01:00–05:00 ET) to prevent stale indicators and reduce manual reconciliation calls.
requirements.source_citation: on Sundays our support team does some manual reconciliation ... so having reliable status syncs after that longer maintenance window is important; otherwise they'll be looking at stale indicators and it causes a lot of calls.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder notes operational pain when status data is stale after maintenance; requires post-maintenance sync/consistency checks. Gaps: expected sync latency and verification steps post-maintenance.
requirements.follow_up_question: What maximum acceptable delay for post-maintenance status synchronization is acceptable, and what verification or reconciliation steps should be automated?

requirements.requirement: Frontend and backend development must adhere to code quality standards (linting and corporate UI lint rules) to reduce developer friction and avoid build/regression issues.
requirements.source_citation: last month I spent an afternoon fixing a styling bug that failed the UI linting rules, which was kind of annoying, but I guess it's necessary.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder experienced developer overhead from failing lint rules; indicates a need for enforced coding/UI standards. Gaps: which linters/rules and whether CI enforcement is required.
requirements.follow_up_question: Which linting and style rules must be enforced, and should CI pipelines block merges on lint failures or only warn?
